notes: NCBI StatPearls Pituitary Apoplexy (last update 2025-09-03) was reread on 2026-08-27 and directly supports sudden pituitary hemorrhage/infarction, abrupt headache/visual/ophthalmoplegic presentation, and acute adrenal insufficiency as the most immediate life-threatening complication.
Endotext Pituitary Apoplexy was reread for sellar-pressure/cavernous-sinus pathophysiology, hyponatremia, low cortisol, and urgent glucocorticoid replacement.

Endotext Diagnosis and Management of Adrenal Insufficiency and ACTH Action on the Adrenals were reread for low ACTH/low cortisol with preserved mineralocorticoid secretion in secondary adrenal insufficiency and RAAS/potassium control of aldosterone.
The official USMLE Content Outline 2026 was visually inspected at Endocrine System page 31 and explicitly lists pituitary apoplexy under pituitary disorders.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

duplicate_gate.diagnosis: Pituitary apoplexy with acute secondary adrenal insufficiency

claim_audit.apoplexy_mechanism: Pituitary apoplexy is sudden hemorrhage or infarction within the pituitary, frequently in a pre-existing adenoma.
claim_audit.neuro_phenotype: Abrupt headache, visual deficits, ophthalmoplegia and ptosis are supported consequences of acute sellar expansion and cavernous-sinus/optic-apparatus involvement.
claim_audit.critical_endocrine_deficit: Acute secondary adrenal insufficiency from loss of ACTH is the most immediately life-threatening endocrine complication and warrants urgent glucocorticoid replacement.
claim_audit.secondary_ai_physiology: ACTH deficiency decreases cortisol while aldosterone remains relatively preserved because mineralocorticoid secretion is regulated primarily by the renin-angiotensin system and serum potassium.
claim_audit.hypotension_mechanism: Cortisol deficiency can cause hypotension through reduced vascular responsiveness to angiotensin II and catecholamines even when aldosterone is preserved.
claim_audit.hyponatremia_pattern: Cortisol deficiency increases ADH-mediated free-water retention and can produce hyponatremia; preserved aldosterone explains the absence of the typical hyperkalemia of primary adrenal insufficiency.
claim_audit.distractor_1: Primary adrenal cortical destruction would impair both cortisol and aldosterone and would more strongly favor hyperkalemia and salt wasting; the lesion here is pituitary.
claim_audit.distractor_2: Posterior pituitary ADH loss produces central diabetes insipidus with free-water loss and a tendency toward hypernatremia rather than the observed hyponatremia.
claim_audit.distractor_3: Central TSH deficiency may coexist after pituitary injury but does not account for the immediate hemodynamic collapse as directly as acute cortisol deficiency.
claim_audit.distractor_4: The apoplexy syndrome causes loss rather than excess of ACTH in the relevant emergency; hypercortisolism does not fit the hypotensive/hypoglycemic pattern.
claim_audit.blueprint_claim: USMLE 2026 explicitly lists pituitary apoplexy under Endocrine System pituitary disorders.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Abrupt retro-orbital headache, vomiting, ophthalmoplegia/ptosis and MRI-confirmed hemorrhagic infarction in a pituitary macroadenoma establish pituitary apoplexy. Hypotension, hypoglycemia and hyponatremia with normal potassium identify acute secondary adrenal insufficiency: ACTH and cortisol fall, while aldosterone is relatively preserved.
adversarial_second_pass.primary_vs_secondary_challenge: The normal potassium is not absolute proof, but it is internally consistent with preserved aldosterone in secondary adrenal insufficiency and makes simultaneous primary cortisol/aldosterone failure less plausible.
adversarial_second_pass.siadh_challenge: Cortisol deficiency itself can promote ADH activity and hyponatremia. SIADH can coexist in CNS disease, but it would not explain the cortisol-dependent shock physiology and hypoglycemia as well as ACTH loss.
adversarial_second_pass.diabetes_insipidus_challenge: Pituitary apoplexy can occasionally affect posterior pituitary function, but central DI would produce polyuria/free-water loss and usually hypernatremia unless intake or treatment obscured it; those findings are absent.
adversarial_second_pass.thyroid_challenge: Acute pituitary injury can lower TSH, but severe central hypothyroidism is not the dominant immediate cause of the classic apoplexy hemodynamic emergency.
adversarial_second_pass.acute_timing_challenge: Although chronic ACTH deficiency leads to zona fasciculata atrophy, pituitary apoplexy is independently recognized as causing acute secondary adrenal insufficiency; the item does not depend on chronic adrenal atrophy.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: Options are mechanistic endocrine explanations of comparable length. The correct answer is not uniquely hedged or excessively detailed and no distractor is nonsensical.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: The item uses clinically plausible laboratory values only to establish a coherent pattern and does not assert a mandatory sodium, potassium, glucose, cortisol, or blood-pressure threshold.
